title: Choose a detecting derivation killing a finite type coefficient subring
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $B$ a domain of characteristic $p$, and $M$ its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose $R_0$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $R_0\to B$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $f\in B$ and let $D:M\to M$ be an additive map satisfying $D(xy)=xD(y)+yD(x)$ with $D(f)\ne0$. There exist a subring $A\subset B$ over which $B$ is of finite type and an additive map $\delta:M\to M$ satisfying the Leibniz rule such that $\delta(a)=0$ for every $a\in A$ and $\delta(f)\ne0$; elements of $B$ are viewed in $M$ by the fraction field map.

source.place: Tag 07PH (lemma-find-D), normalization and coefficient-subfield paragraphs before the final denominator-clearing paragraph

proof.text: The Leibniz power formula gives D(x^p)=0 in characteristic p, so the image of f is not a pth power in M.

Replace the base R0 by its image R in B, using completeness of a proper quotient. The kernel is prime, so R is a complete Noetherian local domain of characteristic p. Cohen structure gives an embedded power series subring S=k[[x1,...,xn]] over a field k with R finite over S; the Cohen ring alternative is impossible in characteristic p. Thus B is finite type over S.

Normalize over S to obtain an embedded polynomial ring C=S[y1,...,ym] and C inside B0 inside B, with B0 finite over C and (B0)_g=B_g for nonzero g in S. Hence Frac(B0)=M and M/Frac(C) is finite. B is still finite type over C because its finite S-algebra generators generate over every intermediate subring.

Choose a p-basis of k. Its finite subsets J give coefficient subrings C_J inside C with C finite over C_J, and fraction subfields K_J with directed intersection K^p, where K=Frac(C). In the finite extension M/K, the intersection of M^p K_J is M^p by the subfield intersection theorem. The image of f is outside M^p, so for some J it is outside M^p K_J. The differential kernel criterion identifies this latter field with the kernel of d:M to Omega_(M/K_J), so df is nonzero there.

Choose an M-linear form nonzero on df and compose it with the universal K_J-derivation. Restrict scalars to the integers to obtain delta; it vanishes on C_J and is nonzero on f. Let A be the embedded image of C_J in B. Since C is finite over C_J and B is finite type over C, B is finite type over A by transitivity. This proves coefficient preparation without constructing a B-valued derivation or clearing denominators.

Given a characteristic p domain finite type over a complete noetherian local ring and a fraction field derivation nonzero on f, choose a detecting derivation killing a subring over which the domain is finite type

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_coefficient_derivation
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CharP B p]
    (M : Type v) [Field M] [Algebra B M] [IsFractionRing B M]
    (R₀ : Type w) [CommRing R₀] [IsNoetherianRing R₀] [IsLocalRing R₀]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀) R₀]
    [Algebra R₀ B] [Algebra.FiniteType R₀ B]
    (f : B) (D : Derivation ℤ M M) (hD : D (algebraMap B M f) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ A : Subring B, Algebra.FiniteType A B ∧
      ∃ δ : Derivation ℤ M M,
        (∀ a : A, δ (algebraMap B M a) = 0) ∧ δ (algebraMap B M f) ≠ 0
